correctness.rationale: Exact Fock matrix identity identifies first Gaussian moments. For distinct balls the difference of normalized defining quadratics separates their symmetric difference and forces a strictly positive moment pairing. Positive-part convex duality gives a unique global minimizer; boundary transport gives determinant r^n lambda^{n+1}det Cov(omega)>0; invariance of domain proves optimal count. The planar Bessel determinant and deterministic numerical checker agree.

value.rationale: A natural finite-parameter inverse Gaussian Gabor aperture problem is solved with exactly the topologically minimal number of accessible Hermite operator coefficients, in every dimension, and a uniquely minimizing convex reconstruction functional and explicit local covariance Jacobian. This is a complete sharp minimal-measurement classification, not just a Gaussian integral evaluation or isolated finite computation.
